sections.h2: Who does what on property tax in Lake County?
sections.html:
Lake County property tax runs through several offices, each with its own question. The Treasurer (847-377-2323) mails the bills, collects payment and passes the money to the districts. The Chief County Assessment Office supervises values, with township assessors doing the local work. Appeals go to the Board of Review. The County Clerk works out the rates and takes over after a tax sale for redemption.

With 18 townships in the county, your township assessor is where a worry about the number on your assessment notice should start. Little of what you pay stays with the county: Lake County government gets about seven percent of an average bill, and school districts take about 69 percent. More than 200 separate taxing bodies levy tax here.

sections.h2: How big is Lake County and what do homes cost there?
sections.html:
Lake County fills the northeast corner of Illinois, touching Wisconsin and Lake Michigan, and Waukegan serves as seat and largest city. Its total area is 1,368 square miles, yet 444 of them are land. No other Illinois county has more water than land.

Residents numbered 714,342 at the 2020 Census, and the July 2025 estimate is 719,339. For 2020 through 2024 the bureau lists a $345,700 median home value, 74.8% of homes lived in by their owners, and $110,416 in median household income. Permits for 1,468 new units came in 2025. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,503, so a bill of several thousand dollars a year is a real line item.

The county lists dozens of cities and villages and many separate elementary and high school districts, so the mix of taxing bodies depends on the parcel. The district maps and the bill itself show which ones apply.

sections.h2: How does the Lake County property tax cycle work?
sections.html:
One cycle spans two years, which means a bill reflects work done the year before. In year one, township assessors set values as of January 1 at one third of fair market value, using three years of sales. The county then equalizes values across townships, mails assessment notices known as blue sheets, and the Board of Review hears appeals. Taxing districts pass budgets and levies during the same year.

In year two, the Board finishes its hearings, the County Clerk figures tax rates from the levies and the final values, and the Treasurer mails bills at the start of May. The county's warning is blunt: by the time you get the bill, it is too late to protest it. The time to speak up is at the assessment notice and at the budget meetings of the taxing districts.

sections.h2: What is the Lake County property tax payment schedule?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in early May, with installments in June and September. The Treasurer's calendar for tax year 2025, collected in 2026, lays out the sequence:

Lake County 2025 real estate tax calendar, payable in 2026 (source: Lake County Treasurer, Real Estate Tax Calendar)
DateEvent
May 1Property tax bills mailed
June 4First installment due
September 4Second installment due; last day to pay at local banks
October 2Last day to pay in the office to avoid publication and final notices
October 22Publication and final notice
November 12Last day to pay to avoid tax sale, by 5:00 p.m., no postmark
November 13Tax sale

The county says the due dates, interest dates and the tax sale date are fixed, while other dates on the calendar may shift for administrative reasons.

sections.h2: What does a late Lake County payment cost, and can you prepay?
sections.html:
Under state law the collector adds 1.5% a month to any unpaid installment, figured on the 5th of the month with no proration. For the 2026 collection, a first installment paid between June 5 and July 4 carried 1.5%, and by the October 5 to November 12 window it reached 7.5%. The second installment started at 1.5% on September 5 and reached 3.0% in the last window.

  • Not receiving a bill, medical emergencies and travel do not qualify for forgiveness of the penalty
  • Forgiveness applies only to a documented Lake County error
  • In the final weeks before the sale, the Treasurer's Office takes only cash or certified funds, in person
  • A December prepayment window lets owners pay up to 50% of the previous year's bill, by check only, with the parcel number in the memo line

Owners who pay through mortgage escrow can look up status on the Treasurer's site by parcel number, though a payment can take weeks to appear as paid.

sections.h2: How does an assessment appeal work in Lake County?
sections.html:
Each township has its own deadline, which falls one month after its assessments are published. The 2026 final filing dates ran from August 24 for Benton and Ela townships to November 2 for Shields. Waukegan's closed September 8, Libertyville's September 21 and Antioch's October 19, and all of those have passed.

The Board urges a conversation with the township assessor beforehand and requires one for factual-error appeals. Appeals are filed online through the Smartfile system. The county names these reasons as typical:

  • A factual error such as the wrong square footage
  • An assessment above one third of the recent sale price
  • An assessment above one third of market value
  • An assessment higher than comparable properties

You may choose a hearing by letter, phone, in person or Zoom, and corporations and LLCs must use an attorney. Hearings are finished in early February. A missed window forfeits the appeal for that year.

sections.h2: Which exemptions reduce a Lake County tax bill?
sections.html:
Exemptions are filed through the Smartfile e-filing portal run by the Chief County Assessment Office, and staff will help by phone or in person.

  • General homestead: takes $8,000 off equalized assessed value for an owner's main residence as of January 1, with no yearly renewal
  • Senior exemption: another $8,000, which can be claimed on top of the general homestead
  • Senior assessment freeze: protects limited-income seniors from increases from rising values, but not from higher tax rates
  • Senior tax deferral: lets qualified seniors defer part or all of the tax on their residence
  • Home improvement, disabled persons and veterans exemptions

Exemptions do not transfer to a newly assigned parcel number, so a split or combined lot needs a fresh application under the new number.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Lake County taxes at the tax sale?
sections.html:
By law the Treasurer sells each year's unpaid taxes, and the sale falls in November after October final notices. The county stresses that the house itself is not sold, just the delinquent taxes. A tax buyer pays them, the districts receive the money, and the owner then works with the County Clerk's Office on redemption.

A seller who owes tax should clear it by closing. The Treasurer can quote the amount due, the County Clerk can estimate redemption for a parcel already sold, and the Treasurer's Office also handles payment status, delinquent prior-year taxes and duplicate bills.

faqs.q: What are the Lake County, Illinois property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed in early May with installments in June and September. For tax year 2025 the dates were June 4 and September 4, 2026.

faqs.q: How much is the penalty on a late Lake County tax payment?
faqs.a: State law adds 1.5% per month to an unpaid installment, counted on the 5th and never prorated. Forgiveness is limited to documented Lake County errors.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Lake County assessment?
faqs.a: One month after your township's assessments are published. In 2026 those dates ranged from August 24 to November 2, depending on the township, and all have passed.

faqs.q: Does Lake County sell the house at the tax sale?
faqs.a: No. Only the unpaid taxes are sold, and the owner then redeems through the County Clerk's Office.

faqs.q: Is there a way to prepay Lake County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, during a December window announced by the Treasurer. Prepayment may be up to 50% of the prior year's bill, by check only, with the parcel number in the memo.
